intro.title: Massawa Urban Heritage: Discover the Rich History of Eritrea's Coastal Gem
intro.text: The city is considered a mosaic carrying in its folds a mixture of residents and dialects

geo.title: Geographical overview of the city of Massawa
geo.text: Massawa is the second most important city and the main port in Eritrea, and it is located on the coast of one of the most important international trade lines, and has been an important historical port for several centuries.

timeline.item4: 1557: The Islamic Ottoman Eyalet of Abyssinia

heritage.title: Urban Heritage of Massawa
heritage.content1: Massawa, known as the "Pearl of the Red Sea," boasts an extraordinary architectural heritage that reflects centuries of diverse cultural influences. From Ottoman coral-block buildings to Italian Renaissance-inspired structures, the city stands as a living testament to the region's rich history.
heritage.content2: The old town, with its narrow winding streets and historic buildings, represents one of the most significant urban heritage sites in East Africa. Despite challenges from natural disasters and conflict, the city's architectural treasures continue to inspire preservation efforts.

about.title: From Exile to Homecoming: Rediscovering Massawa's Urban Heritage
about.description: An Eritrean civil initiative that seeks to document and protect the urban heritage of Massawa

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.content: A future where Massawa's heritage sites are fully restored, accessible to all, and serve as a source of pride, education, and sustainable economic development for local communities.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.content: To preserve, protect, and promote the architectural and cultural heritage of Massawa through professional restoration, comprehensive documentation, community education, and international collaboration.

passion.title: Passion
passion.description: Deep commitment to preserving cultural identity and architectural beauty.

community.title: Community
